classification.difficultyReason: Development: complete two linked datasets in a back-to-back plot, preserving repetitions, zero leaves and opposite ordering, then compare overall rainfall. These are routine linked applications of the taught construction and reading methods.

inlines.text: The average rainfall in millimetres for Adelaide and Melbourne are shown in the table.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Complete the back-to-back stem-and-leaf plot for the rainfall data.

spec.description: Melbourne leaves to the left, central stems, Adelaide leaves to the right. Outer headings have two lines. Fourteen separate dotted writing positions replace source solid blanks. No key.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source-supplied stems and leaves are visible. All fourteen missing leaves remain blank.

answer.short: Missing leaves: stem 1, Adelaide: 7, 9; stem 3, Adelaide: 8, 8; stem 4, Melbourne: 9; stem 5, Melbourne: 9, 9, 8, 8, 2, 1, 0 and Adelaide: 9; stem 6, Adelaide: 5.
answer.worked: Use the tens digit as the stem and the units digit as the leaf. Retain repeated values. Adelaide’s leaves increase to the right; Melbourne’s leaves increase away from the stem to the left. The completed plot shows all twelve monthly values for each city.

spec.description: Complete back-to-back rainfall plot, retaining all supplied leaves and all repeated observations.
spec.answerVisibility: Complete answer figure; all fourteen missing leaves are supplied.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Which city receives more rainfall overall?

answer.worked:
Adding the twelve monthly values gives Adelaide a total of 450 mm and Melbourne a total of 660 mm.
$$660-450=210\text{ mm}$$
Melbourne receives 210 mm more rainfall overall.
